# fleet-map

A project's workstreams drawn as a metro map. The spine is the order of milestones (order, not time). Each workstream
is a coloured line that feeds the spine station it serves. Stacked PRs and sub-streams branch off at junctions, side
work sits on sidings, and later work is greyed out. The page is static and opens from `file://`.

**Generated files are copies.** `index.html` and `fleet-map.data.js` begin with: "generated by pij fleet-map from
skills/pij/tools/fleet-map; edits here are overwritten; change the template in the pij repo". To change the page,
edit `templates/index.html` here, in the pij repo. The tool refuses any `--out`, `--dir` or `--structure` inside this
folder, so a project's copy can never edit the skill.

## Verbs

```sh
pij fleet-map init [--dir <d>]       # write the starter structure; refuses to overwrite one
pij fleet-map generate [--structure <p>] [--out <d>] [--at <iso>] [--offline] [--project <slug>]
pij fleet-map open [--out <d>] [--launch]   # print the page's file:// URL; --launch opens it
```

Run them in a project's repo with no flags:

- **The structure** is `<government-root>/fleet-map/fleet-map.structure.json`, where `<government-root>` is the
  `.harness/government` folder of the repo's one worktree on branch `prime-governance`. It is hand-kept, so commit it
  there. A repo laid out another way gets a refusal that prints the `--structure` form to use.
- **The output** is `<main checkout>/scratch/fleet-map/`. The tool warns when that folder isn't git-ignored, and it
  never commits.

It's a one-shot command, with no loop and no daemon. Each run makes one `pij list`, one `pij directory`, and, per PR,
one `gh pr view` and one `pij outputs`.

## The structure

```jsonc
{
  "title": "My project",
  "focus": "first-release",            // spine station the page opens on (default: the first "now")
  "spine": [{ "id": "first-release", "name": "First release", "state": "now", "note": "…" }],  // done|now|next|later
  "lines": [{
    "id": "001", "name": "Core", "colour": "#E5194B", "state": "now",
    "joins": "first-release",           // a spine station; or "joinsLine": "<line id>", "at": "<stop id>"
    "roadmap": "001-core",
    "repo": "owner/name",               // optional: its PRs live in another repo; a stop's "repo" overrides
    "roles": [{ "role": "pm" }, { "role": "coder", "seats": ["pij-…"] }],   // the line's Pij Community
    "stops": [{
      "id": "api", "name": "API", "pr": 42, "owner": "pij-…", "waitingOn": "Reviewer verdict", "note": "…",
      "state": "review",                // merged|review|building|blocked|held|waiting|next|later|closed
      "stops": [ /* one level of stacked stops */ ]
    }]
  }],
  "sidings": [ /* lines that dead-end: side work */ ],
  "depot": { "name": "Depot", "roles": [{ "role": "pa" }] }   // shared roles, once, beside the spine
}
```

A stop with `pr` takes its state, head, title and verdicts from live sources; `state` covers what they don't know. A
`repo` (`owner/name`, on a line or a stop; stacked stops inherit it) sends that PR's lookup to `gh pr view <n> -R
owner/name`. A value that isn't `owner/name` is a warning, and its PRs aren't looked up. A role with no `seat` or
`seats` shows the directory's live holders. `templates/structure.example.json` is the starter.

## Live data: pij first

- **Seats** come from `pij list --json`: state, plus context rounded to 1k.
- **Role holders** and each role's latest output come from `pij directory --json`.
- **Verdicts** come from `pij outputs --subject pr:<n> --json`. For each role it shows the newest verdict, preferring
  one at the PR's head, and flags a verdict given at an older head.
  - PR comment verdicts (the old comment shapes) fill in only for roles pij has no verdict for. Where both exist,
    pij wins.
  - A PR in another repo (a `repo` set) takes its verdicts from its PR comments only. pij output subjects
    (`pr:<n>`) name the project's own PRs, so `pr:7` would be the wrong PR.
- **`gh pr view`** adds state, head, base, title and URL. If gh is missing or fails, that becomes a warning in the
  data, never an error, and each verdict shows its sha without claiming it is current or older.
- **`--offline`** skips every live source.

## Determinism

- **Data:** keys are sorted and arrays keep the structure's order, so an unchanged world gives a byte-identical file.
  `generatedAt` is the only field that moves; pin it with `--at`.
- **Colour:** a line without a `colour` gets one from a fixed palette, picked by FNV-1a of its id. The tool writes it
  back into the project's structure, so it never changes.
- **Layout:** the layout is a pure function of the data.
  - Stops sit at a fixed pitch, and lanes at a fixed pitch.
  - Lanes are allocated first-fit, claiming label and nameplate widths.
  - Labels wrap by character count.
  - There is no randomness and no font measurement, so the SVG is the same at any width.

## Reading the map

- **Track:** solid where the work is merged.
  - Up to a line's first open stop it is solid; a train marks that point.
  - A stop merged out of order has solid track around it, so the gap shows only at the open stops.
  - Everything else is a cased "under construction" rail.
- **Active work:** in review has a solid green ring with a magnifier. Building has a dashed ring with a spanner. The
  now station has a green halo. Moving dots run from active stops toward the spine and stop at a blocked, held or
  waiting stop.
- **Waiting on Jordan:** an amber diamond with a J. "Your move: N" steps through them.
- **Pij Community:** each line's nameplate carries role chips with live dots. Hover a chip for its seat, state,
  context and last output. Shared roles sit in the depot. "Who's awake" dims stops whose owner isn't working.
- **Navigation:** drag, scroll, pinch, the `+`/`-` keys, `0` to fit and `N` for now. The minimap and the collapsible
  key help with big maps. A fully merged line is drawn quieter, as history.

Tests: `harness/scripts/fleet-map.test.ts`, with the fixture and golden data in `harness/fixtures/fleet-map/`.
